questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
questions.answer:
The SI unit of resistivity is
\[
\Omega\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: State the relation between conductivity \(\sigma\) and resistivity \(\rho\).
questions.answer:
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity:
\[
\sigma=\frac{1}{\rho}
\]

questions.prompt: For an ohmic material with positive resistivity, are \(\vec E\) and \(\vec J\) parallel or anti-parallel?
questions.answer:
For an ohmic material,
\[
\vec E=\rho\vec J
\]
With \(\rho>0\), \(\vec E\) and \(\vec J\) are parallel.

questions.prompt: A material has conductivity \(5.0\times10^7\,\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}\). Find its resistivity.
A wire has length \(2.0\,\mathrm{m}\), area \(1.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^2}\), and resistivity \(2.5\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\). Find \(V/I\).
A metal has \(\rho_0=1.6\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\) at \(20^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and \(\alpha=4.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{K^{-1}}\). Estimate \(\rho\) at \(70^\circ\mathrm{C}\).
A cylindrical wire is stretched to twice its original length while its volume stays constant. Assuming resistivity is unchanged, by what factor does \(V/I\) change?
questions.answer:
For fixed volume,
\[
AL=\mathrm{constant}
\]
If length doubles,
\[
L'=2L
\]
then area halves:
\[
A'=\frac{A}{2}
\]
Since
\[
\frac{V}{I}=R=\rho\frac{L}{A}
\]
the factor change is
\[
\frac{R'}{R}=\frac{(2L)/(A/2)}{L/A}=4
\]
So \(V/I\) increases by a factor of \(4\).

questions.prompt: A conductor is tapered so its cross-sectional area varies as \(A(x)=A_0(1+x/L)\) from \(x=0\) to \(L\). With resistivity \(\rho\), derive the resistance by integrating small slices.
questions.answer:
Treat the conductor as slices of thickness \(dx\):
\[
dR=\rho\frac{dx}{A(x)}
\]
With
\[
A(x)=A_0\left(1+\frac{x}{L}\right)
\]
\[
R=\int_0^L \rho\frac{dx}{A_0(1+x/L)}
\]
\[
R=\frac{\rho}{A_0}\int_0^L\frac{dx}{1+x/L}
\]
Let \(u=1+x/L\), so \(dx=L\,du\), with limits \(1\) to \(2\):
\[
R=\frac{\rho L}{A_0}\int_1^2\frac{du}{u}
\]
\[
R=\frac{\rho L}{A_0}\ln2
\]

questions.prompt: A wire has \(\rho(T)=\rho_0[1+\alpha(T-T_0)]\) and temperature varies linearly from \(T_0\) at one end to \(T_0+\Delta T\) at the other. Derive the resistance for uniform area \(A\) and length \(L\).
questions.answer:
For uniform area,
\[
dR=\rho(T(x))\frac{dx}{A}
\]
The temperature varies linearly:
\[
T(x)-T_0=\Delta T\frac{x}{L}
\]
so
\[
\rho(x)=\rho_0\left[1+\alpha\Delta T\frac{x}{L}\right]
\]
Then
\[
R=\frac{1}{A}\int_0^L \rho_0\left[1+\alpha\Delta T\frac{x}{L}\right]dx
\]
\[
R=\frac{\rho_0}{A}\left[L+\frac{\alpha\Delta T}{L}\frac{L^2}{2}\right]
\]
\[
R=\frac{\rho_0L}{A}\left(1+\frac{\alpha\Delta T}{2}\right)
\]
This is the same as using the average temperature rise \(\Delta T/2\) in the linear model.
